rules.question: How does an INI loader word a line it refuses (no =, unknown key, bad value)?
rules.owner: ini_not_key_value_text, ini_unknown_key_text and ini_bad_value_text in src/app/ini_errors.h
rules.pattern: is not key = value|unknown key \\"" \+|\\" is not " \+
must_match: throw RulesFileError(where + ": \"" + text + "\" is not key = value");
throw RulesFileError(path + ": " + key + " = \"" + value + "\" is not " + want);
rules.note: hydra_rules.ini and hydra_settings.ini once each built these three error lines; both call the helper now, so a third loader that builds them by hand is flagged. Decided by: D270 call 4.

rules.question: Is this text a whole number that fits an int?
rules.note: The rules file, the settings file and hydra_replay's --cap each had their own copy of the test (a finite number with no fraction that fits an int); all three call parse_whole_number now. Decided by: D270 call 4.

rules.question: What does a command-line tool do when hydra_settings.ini is refused?

exempt.why: The app answers a different question on purpose: it keeps running on the defaults and saves nothing (AppState::settings_error) instead of exiting.

must_not_match: if (const int code = hydra::app::load_tool_settings(settings, legacy_fills)) return code;
rules.note: hydra_batch, hydra_fillcompare and hydra_bench each caught the loader's error and printed it on their own. They call load_tool_settings now, as the rules file's tools call load_tool_rules, so a fourth tool that catches it itself is flagged. Decided by: D270 call 4.
